chapter_theme: Sivavakkiyar sets the letters of Om and of சிவாயம் against every outward form of religion: the Lord who takes shape in அ, உ and ம, who joins life and body and who dances the whirling cosmoses into one, is to be known inside the body, not in a shaped stone, a hauled chariot, a staff and caste, or a stack of books. Between the attacks run riddling questions to the 'gnanis' about seed, womb and mantra, and a yogic ascent through the six lotuses to a space where 'he is, and I am not'.
structure_note: No commentary orders the chapter. Three verses end with the challenge to the knowers to explain (1190, 1200, 1213); 1193 and 1194 are one sentence split across two units; the polemical verses (1195, 1198, 1199, 1204 to 1207, 1210, 1212) alternate with verses of pervasion and praise (1192, 1197, 1203, 1209, 1211).

1189.reading: In the cause that is A he stood as many forms, in the cause that is U he took shape, in the cause that is M the world is bewildered, and in the cause that is Si it became clear: Sivayam.
1189.nuance: The sense turns on the four letters. அ, உ and ம are the parts of Om; சி is the first letter of சிவாயம். Tradition reads A as the Lord's manifold creation, U as his taking form, M as the world's delusion in matter, and the letter of Siva's own name as the clarity that resolves them. On that reading the five-letter mantra is set above Om.

1190.reading: Did U enter the letter A and A come to birth? Did the letters U and M stand each within the other? If they stand evenly matched, even when the states of Siva are reached, you gnanis of good nature must explain it at length.
1190.nuance: A series of questions about how the three parts of Om relate, closed by the challenge to the knowers that recurs in 1200 and 1213. மிவ்வை is an unusual word; the editors' gloss takes it as good quality, so the address is 'you knowers of good nature'. Whether the questions are rhetorical or sincere is left open.

1191.reading: The substance that stands filling the primal five, the beginningless four, the luminous three, the formless two and the single just one: that primal one, which has none of them, is the five letters.
1191.nuance: The numbers are coded. Tradition takes the five as the elements or the five letters themselves, the four as the Vedas or the four kinds of birth, the three as sun, moon and fire, the two as Siva and Shakti or sun and moon, and the one as the Lord. அற்ற தஞ்செழுத்து can mean the five letters 'that have shed' all these, or the one that is 'without' them is the five letters; either way the mantra and the Lord are identified.

1192.reading: There is nothing without sky, yet when you enter it there is no sky; nothing without flesh, yet no flesh; nothing without 'I', yet when you approach there is no 'I'; there is nothing without the Self, and it dances, shimmering.
1192.nuance: Each term both pervades everything and vanishes on inspection; only தான் (the Self, or He) remains, and what it does is dance. The verse makes the dance, not a substance, the last word about what is.

1193.reading: Thinking on the letter with the curl, setting it at the mouth of speech, passing beyond pain and pleasure, going through the channel they speak of, raising the fire of the firm akshara, and crossing the six lotuses, in the space beyond ...
1193.nuance: The sentence runs on into 1194. சுழித்ததோர் எழுத்து, the letter with a curl, is taken by tradition as Om (or its ஓ); அக்கிரம் may be அக்ஷரம், the letter, or அக்ர, the tip or crown; the fire raised and the six lotuses crossed are the serpent power and the six supports in the yogic body. The verse describes an ascent through the central channel in the Siddhars' usual terms without naming them.

1194.reading: ... when the drooping eye is gathered and one arrives there, where all the letters have yielded their conjuring, in the space that is release, when one presses in and, the mind dazed, experiences it: then He is, I am not, and no one is.
1194.nuance: The second half of 1193. இந்திரசாலம் (Indra's net, conjuring) is what the letters produce; the space beyond it is called வீடு, release. The closing state is given in plain words: he remains, the 'I' does not. விழுத்தகண் is unclear, perhaps the eye turned inward or closed.

1195.reading: You run about seeking fine bathing waters; the fine bathing and the Lord are within us. If, seeking the bathing at the limit, you perform the single worship, the soul that reaches Tillai dances within Siva's state.
1195.nuance: மஞ்சனம் is the bathing water of a deity or a holy bath. எல்லைமஞ்சனம், the bath 'at the limit', is obscure; tradition takes it as an inner bathing at the body's end, the crown. Tillai (Chidambaram) is named as something the soul reaches inside, so the dance in the hall is placed within.

1196.reading: Life stands within before it takes a body; life becomes A and the body becomes U, and what joins life and body is that Siva; I have told how life took up a body.
1196.nuance: The letters are mapped onto the pair life and body, with Siva as the joining; the third letter is not named. In the Tirumanthiram the same letters are read as Siva and Shakti, so the poet's mapping is his own and not the inherited one.

1197.reading: While the seven cosmic spheres whirl, the endless wombs whirl, old Mal with Ayan spread out and whirl, and the dark Shakti standing beyond the eight directions whirls, the cosmoses as one, the primal dance is danced.
1197.nuance: The whirling (உழல) of worlds, wombs, gods and even Shakti is contrasted with the one dance that holds them. இருண்ட சத்தி, the dark Shakti, is perhaps maya or the goddess in her dark form; the verse does not say.

1198.reading: You fools like ghosts: will the great path that was given shape with water and limbs speak? Know within yourselves, as your own right, the God whom dark Mal and Ayan could not see.
1198.nuance: The first half is unclear. பெரியபாதை, 'the great road', may be the body, shaped from water (seed) with its limbs, which cannot speak of God; or a great ritual way. The second half is firm: the God invisible even to Vishnu and Brahma is to be realised inside, and உரிமையாக makes it one's own right.

1199.reading: You call a stone that was made the ancient substance and recite what names, you poor ones; take into your heart instead the One who became able to make, to create, to protect what was created, and so ruled the world.
1199.nuance: பண்ணிவைத்த கல், the stone someone made, against the one who makes: the charge is confusing the made with the maker. நெஞ்சில் உண்ணும், eat him into the heart, is the alternative to naming him.

1200.reading: As the fourfold womb and the bindu that is spoken of become one and settle and contract inside the banyan seed, so is the arising from the womb, the mantra that is spoken: you gnanis above, explain it at length.
1200.nuance: நாலதான போனி (யோனி) is perhaps the four kinds of birth (egg, sweat, sprout and womb); the banyan seed is the stock image of a whole tree folded in a seed. சூலதான உற்பனம் can be 'the origin from pregnancy' (சூல்) or 'the origin bearing the trident' (சூலம்), Siva's; the verse likens the mantra's unfolding to conception either way.

1201.reading: When you were formless, Mother, I did not know you there; when you were in form I knew you; made clear by the guru, becoming flawless knowledge, when the season ripened it became the supreme Brahman.
1201.nuance: The formless is known only through form, and the form named is the guru. அன்னை addresses the Lord as Mother, so the Shakti and the Lord are not distinguished; பருவம், the ripe season, makes knowledge a matter of readiness rather than effort.

1202.reading: Being born and dying, and remaining unborn; forgetting and remembering, and making clear what was hidden; renouncing and giving, and scooping up pleasure; being born and dying: all are contained in the house one was born into.
1202.nuance: பிறந்தவீடு can be the body, the house one is born into, in which every opposite plays out; or the release (வீடு) that has 'been born', in which they all end. The list pairs opposites so that neither side is preferred.

1203.reading: He is in the eye; he is the Mal who churned the dark sea; he is in the sky and stands reaching there; he who made the earth is within himself; he is within me and stands as everything everywhere.
1203.nuance: The Lord is named as Mal (Vishnu, churner of the ocean) without any sectarian edge, as in 1197 and 1198 where Mal and Ayan are the lesser gods. The series moves from eye to sky to self to 'within me' before 'everywhere'.

1204.reading: Though you seek goats and lands, elephants and armies, a crore of horses, will any of them come and stand beside you? The alms thrown as you ran and the dharma done gladly: that dharma comes and stands like a horse that has bolted and returned.
1204.nuance: வாசி here is a horse, not the breath of the Siddhars' வாசி yoga. The image is of a horse set loose at a gallop coming back to stand before its owner: what one has given returns, what one owns does not follow.

1205.reading: Sesame, iron, blankets, cotton and bronze, garments, coin and cloth for the Lord: if you give fitting gifts to the Vedic one who dwells within, slowly every disease turns back, Sivayam.
1205.nuance: The list is the standard set of gifts made to Brahmins at planetary rites (sesame, iron and a blanket are Saturn's). The verse redirects them to உள்ளிருக்கும் வேதியர், the Vedic one within, which is the Lord in the body or an inner priest; whether the promise about disease is sincere or mocks the rite's own promise is not settled by the words.

1206.reading: People of the town, you gather as one mind, set a copper image on the chariot, tie on the rope and haul it; look, look at the uproar that quarrelling men make over the primal Siddha-Lord whom no one can know.
1206.nuance: The scene is a temple car festival with its processional bronze. புரளி is a disturbance or a lie; போரிலான is unclear, perhaps 'men given to fighting'. The Lord is called ஆதி சித்தநாதர், the first Siddha, the title the poets give themselves.

1207.reading: Men bewildered by a mind that delusion has entered: if you can swim across with the mantra the guru gave, well; otherwise the servants and the child will suffer the twelve toils that cotton suffers.
1207.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are obscure. பருத்தி பட்ட பாடு is proverbial for the many processes cotton goes through before it is cloth, here counted as twelve, perhaps the toils of rebirth. குருக்கொடுத்த தொண்டர் and முகனொடித்த பிள்ளை (the servants who gave the guru, the child with the broken face) may be corrupt.

1208.reading: In the mother's womb-chamber, as the brightness of fire, coming into that chamber as a rare form, when it stood like itself it cut the obstruction and became open, gave golden fine greatness and grew as the master.
1208.nuance: The embryo is a light of fire that grows into தலைவன், the lord. தடையறுத்து வெளியதாய் can be read plainly as birth, breaking out into the open, or yogically as the light cutting its block and becoming space; the verse allows both.

1209.reading: Can I forget you for even a moment, the unveiled light that dwells in my heart and hides me, the peerless Lord of great light called gold? Grant me birthlessness at your golden feet.
1209.nuance: A plea in the middle of polemic. மறைப்பிலாத சோதி is the light without veil; எனை மறைப்பு, that it hides me, may mean it covers the poet with itself.

1210.reading: Is the staff you grip your own, you madmen who claim to be Brahman? Having dropped the gross guise, do you take up distinctions of caste? If you can speak truly of the Siva you have distilled, you may go and join the Lord.
1210.nuance: Addressed to staff-bearing renouncers who say 'I am Brahman' yet keep caste; the staff that is 'not yours' says that a renouncer owns nothing, caste included. திடுக்கமுற்ற ஈசன், the startled Lord, is odd; it may be a corruption of திடமுற்ற, the firm Lord.

1211.reading: You are Shakti, you are compassion, you are the sound of the hesitant conch; you are siddhi, you are Siva, you are the letters that are Sivaya; you are release, the first, the three gods: know and realise the city of bones within yourselves.
1211.nuance: அத்திபூரம் is the uncertain word: taken as அஸ்திபுரம், the city of bones, it is the body, and the verse ends by placing all it has listed inside it; it could also be a shrine's name. The conch's sound is the inner nada of 1227.

1212.reading: You cheats of the sastras in coats and glittering beads, you liars who pile up books and recite doctrine: what is your fixity, what your knowledge? Say, what is the letter you abide in and what its mark, you treacherous deceivers?
1212.nuance: நிட்டை (nishtha) is settled absorption, set against learning. பட்டை can be the stripe of ash on the brow or the outer bark of a thing; 'the letter you stood in' asks which syllable they have actually realised, not which they recite.

1213.reading: That the true semen was the means; that it turned white and quickly became water within the water; that the cool body wore it and became a form: you clear gnanis, explain this clearly.
1213.nuance: The third of the challenge verses. It traces the body from சுக்கிலம் (seed) through fluid to form and asks the knowers to account for it; whether the question is a test or a confession of wonder is open.

links.note: Both read the letters of Om as a pair joined by a third. Sivavakkiyar makes A life and U the body, joined by Siva; Tirumular makes A the Lord and U the Lady spread through the world, rising together as sound. The same letters carry two different pairs.

Both say that nothing one owns goes along with one and only the deed does. The Naladiyar says it of all deeds at death; Sivavakkiyar says it of gifts and dharma, which return like a bolted horse while elephants, armies and horses do not.

Both take the gifts customarily made to Brahmins and redirect them: Tirumular to the ash-wearing devotee, worth more than feeding ten million Vedic Brahmins; Sivavakkiyar to 'the Vedic one who dwells within', the Lord in the body.

The Kural says birth is alike for all and distinction comes only from what one does; Sivavakkiyar mocks renouncers who claim to be Brahman yet keep caste distinctions. Both deny that caste marks anything real.

Tirumular says that for those who set Nandi firmly in love there is no caste; Sivavakkiyar says that those who claim to be Brahman cannot also keep caste. Both make caste fall away at the point of realisation, Tirumular by grace and Sivavakkiyar by consistency.

Both separate owning books from understanding them. The Naladiyar distinguishes scholars who keep books from those who understand and teach; Sivavakkiyar calls those who stack books and recite liars, and asks what fixity and knowledge they have.

Tirumular says those who recite many praises and hymns lack understanding and wither within; Sivavakkiyar asks the reciters of sastra what letter they actually abide in. Both set realised knowledge above recitation.

Both trace the body from the white seed through the womb to its form. Tirumular gives the measures (eight finger-breadths in, four out, a body of eight spans); Sivavakkiyar gives the stages (seed, water, form) and asks the knowers to explain them.

Tirumular says siddhi, release and true knowledge cannot be known unless the Lord takes form and gives grace; Sivavakkiyar says he did not know the formless Mother until she came in form, and names the guru as the form that made it clear.

Both set the Lord's real form against the installed image: Tirumular makes earth the pedestal, sky the linga and the sea its bathing hall; Sivavakkiyar calls those who name a made stone the ancient substance poor fools and points to the maker. Tirumular elsewhere defends the temple (516), so the agreement is on where the Lord's form is, not on whether to worship the stone.

Both describe the ascent through the central channel: Tirumular through the sushumna in the narrowed stalk of the eight-petalled flower to the gathered light; Sivavakkiyar through the channel, raising the fire and crossing the six lotuses to the space beyond. The vocabulary differs, the route is the same.

source_issues: 1193 and 1194 are one sentence split across two units; 1193 has no main verb.
1190 மிவ்வை is an unusual word; the editors' gloss takes it as good quality.
1198 line 1 and 2: பெரியபாதை பேசுமோ is unclear in syntax and sense.
1207 lines 3 and 4 (குருக்கொடுத்த தொண்டரும் முகனொடித்த பிள்ளையும்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
1210 திடுக்கமுற்ற ஈசனை (the startled Lord) is odd; perhaps திடமுற்ற.
